area: near Lynwood and Height streets, south Bakersfield
disposition: multi-engine response, patient on far side of train
summary: A train struck a pedestrian near the rail line off Lynwood and Height streets in south Bakersfield, drawing a multi-engine response — engines 37, 34 and 33 with Battalion 3. Crews worked access around the train to reach the patient on the far side.

disposition: pedestrian down, video surveillance being archived
summary: A vehicle-versus-pedestrian collision downtown left the pedestrian down at the scene; the pedestrian was described as a female on probation or supervised release. Officers had surveillance video archived for the investigation.

disposition: man struck woman, tried to take infant
summary: A man struck a woman and attempted to take an infant before officers arrived, with a kitchen knife mentioned on the air; the subject was described as a 34-year-old Hispanic man in a white t-shirt and gray shorts. A heavy-duty response was requested.

A burglary at a furniture business on Baker Street had suspects possibly still inside, with a silver Prius spotted in an alleyway nearby. Officers set a perimeter at Baker and Kentucky with a second boundary at Baker and Jackson.

A person in crisis on Di Giorgio Road reportedly made threats against family members and was possibly in possession of a knife, with a child present in the residence. The reporting party said an uncle had seen the knife.

disposition: victim locked in room with children
summary: A domestic violence call on Haley Street had the reporting party locked in a room with children after a disturbance involving the daughter's boyfriend.

disposition: juvenile with visible injuries, possible abuse
summary: A welfare check in the 1200 block of East 18th Street found a juvenile with visible injuries possibly inflicted by a family member; eight other juveniles were in the residence.
A disturbance at a Washington Avenue apartment involved an ex-girlfriend who arrived in a red Dodge and was described as possibly highly volatile.

agency: Kern County Fire Department / Bakersfield Police Department
summary: An automatic fire alarm at a Greenfield preschool on South Union Avenue; the business also reported a burglary, with the situation stable to the rear of the building.
Flooding inside a home on Pinehurst Drive had occupants evacuating.
Crews checked a semi reported to be smoking on Highway 58 near the 223 area, continuing toward Keene; no fire was found.
A male subject in a gray and white shirt was reported possibly attempting to siphon gas from a vehicle on South Union Avenue.
Vehicles were reported racing in the area of a Columbus Street big-box store.
A domestic violence call in the Metro Zone on South Brown Street reported a victim being prevented from leaving.

agency: Kern County Fire Department / Hall Ambulance
summary: A medical aid at a back house on Palm Avenue drew Engine 31.
A domestic violence incident that just occurred on Myers Ranch Court; a suspect description was broadcast.
A 911 caller on Lum Avenue tried to report a domestic incident, then disconnected.
A suspicious person — a female with blonde hair in dark clothing — was reported at a Motel 6 on Western Drive.
A family disturbance on Dolores Street involved a woman and her stepfather.
A fire near Monica Street drew a Station 42 assignment — Engine 42, Patrol 42, Engine 345 and Battalion 4.

agency: Kern County Fire Department / Hall Ambulance
summary: A medical aid at an apartment on Pacific Street drew a Code 2 response with Kern County Sheriff's Office en route alongside Hall Ambulance.
